requirements.requirement: node1 boots with the kernel parameter audit=1, and the setting persists across reboots.
requirements.summary: The executor added audit=1 to every installed boot entry, performed a bounded reboot, and observed a changed boot ID. After recovery, /proc/cmdline contained audit=1, auditctl reported enabled 1, auditd was active, the system was running, and all boot entries retained audit=1.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel, using software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: Before and after the change, node1 ran RHEL 9.8 with kernel 5.14.0-687.20.1.el9_8. The change used the platform-installed native grubby utility, and package health remained intact.

overall_summary: All material outcomes are satisfied. Direct transition evidence shows a healthy baseline, acknowledged reboot and temporary loss of connectivity, a different post-reboot identity, recovered system and auditd service, an active audit=1 kernel setting, persistent boot configuration, and an unchanged RHEL release and kernel. Fixed lifecycle observations independently corroborate the reboot and preserved platform.
limitations: The restart evidence covers node health, auditd, boot configuration, and platform state; no separate application data or multi-node cluster state existed in the supplied single-node task context to verify.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. The grubby update directly established the required persistent parameter (cmd-b5135a8c3f1c4170), and the scheduled reboot directly tested persistence and fulfilled the restart protocol (cmd-7fbebfa8c2c141e9). All other commands were read-only verification or connection polling. Afterward there were no failed services, no new network exposure, healthy package state, and only expected reboot-related PID and systemd-private-directory changes.
